attributes.context: Section 103 defines technological change as the use of automation, machines, computers, robots, software, tablets, or other handheld devices that replace, substitute, or materially change how employees work, and it sets a notice and impact-bargaining framework for technology introduced after the Agreement's effective date.

The surrounding sub-section provides job postings, extra work, seniority/continuous service, probation, health insurance, and severance for employees displaced due to technological change at Viceroy-operated hotels.

extraction_text: Any employee displaced due to technological change shall be entitled to recall to the classification from which the employee was displaced for twenty-four (24) months following the date of displacement and to preference for other job openings at the Hotel where the new technology is implemented in or out of the bargaining unit, after all other preferences possessed by incumbent employees at the Hotel have been exercised but before new employees are hired, provided the employee is qualified for the position or can be qualified in a reasonable period of time with adequate training provided by the Employer. Preference In hiring also will be given to any employee displaced due to technological change, who applies for another position for which he or she is qualified, at other Viceroy-operated hotels subject to a collective bargaining agreement with the Union.

attributes.context: The preceding sentence in the same sub-section addresses recall of employees displaced under the technological change provision and the recognition of Hotel seniority and continuous service for vacation/PTO and health insurance.

extraction_text: If an employee displaced by technological change is hired into a new position at other Viceroy-operated hotels subject to a collective bargaining agreement with the Union, the provisions of that Hotel's collective bargaining agreement shall apply.

attributes.context: It is subsection (b) of Section 103, "Technology," and follows subsection (a), which defines technological change as the use of automation, machines, computers, robots, software, tablets, or other handheld devices that affect the type or manner of work performed by employees.

extraction_text: The Employer shall provide the Union at least a sixty (60) day notice before implementation of any plans to upgrade, modify, improve, or extend technology currently in use by bargaining unit employees that are made after the effective date of this Agreement. The Employer shall provide the Union at least a sixty (60) day advance notice prior to the implementation of any new technological change, occurring after the effective date of this Agreement, that replaces or substitutes for or materially increases or decreases the type or manner of work performed by employees in the Employer's workplace.

attributes.context: It is subsection (c) of Section 103, "Technology," and follows subsection (b), which requires the Employer to give the Union at least sixty (60) days' notice before implementing upgrades to current technology or any new technological change that affects the work performed by employees.

extraction_text: If the Union requests to bargain, it must do so within fifteen (15) days of the Employer's notice and shall include any information requests with such notice. The Employer shall promptly negotiate the impact of the new technology on the bargaining unit employees and the work they perform.

attributes.context: It follows a dispute-resolution sequence in which the parties meet for thirty days and may request federal mediation if the issue is unresolved.

extraction_text: 4. The Employer shall not Implement any technology during such negotiations, but the Employer shall have the right to implement the technology upon the expiration of this ninety (90) day period. The Employer shall not implement any technology unless the Employer has carried out these duties to the Union.

attributes.context: It refers to a preceding notice-and-negotiation sequence for technology implementation, including a 30-day meeting period and optional federal mediation.

extraction_text: (d) This notice and negotiation process shall be the sole and exclusive procedure for resolving disputes over the implementation of new technology. Any disputes arising out of this process shall be subject to the grievance and arbitration process under this Agreement. The arbitrator, however, shall have no authority to order any particular outcome to the bargaining process.

attributes.context: It is part of benefits protections for employees displaced by new technology during a six-month period.

extraction_text: (j) The Employer shall continue to make contributions to the applicable health insurance plan for any employee displaced as a result of the implementation of new technology, at the minimum level necessary to maintain existing benefits under the applicable health plan for six (6) months following the date of displacement.

attributes.context: It addresses classifications affected by technological changes and operation or training when new technology requires human machine operation.

extraction_text: (I) If technological changes reduce the duties of a classification without eliminating them, the classification shall continue to exist, but the Employer may adjust staffing levels, full or part-time status, or after bargaining with the Union the Employer may consolidate existing classifications or distribute the remaining duties to other bargaining unit classifications. If new technology performs functions previously performed by bargaining unit employees and requires human operation of machines, the machines shall be operated by bargaining unit employees and the Employer shall train employees in the affected classification to operate new technology.
